headline: Authors report unified likelihood-based training with accuracy, coverage and retention tradeoffs
summary: A 67-page preprint frames pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning and suitable reinforcement-learning updates as likelihood fitting over a time-varying mixture of static data and successful model-generated targets. Its shared objective and trainer allow those sources to overlap; conventional staged training is a special case. The authors report controlled 124M-parameter reasoning-puzzle experiments and heterogeneous-data experiments with a 0.76B-parameter model. They report better accuracy, coverage, retention or continual-learning outcomes in several evaluated settings, alongside task and schedule tradeoffs. The paper explicitly describes the results as small-scale and does not establish predictive scaling laws or a universally preferred data mixture.
